sections.title: What is LIC Single Premium Endowment Plan (917/717/817)?

content.text: The LIC Single Premium Endowment Plan (UIN: 512N283V03) is a straightforward savings-cum-protection plan where you pay the premium only once at the start of the policy. It's a hassle-free, one-time investment that provides a combination of guaranteed savings and life insurance coverage. Compare this with our LIC premium calculator for other payment options and our LIC maturity calculator to estimate your final benefits. At the end of the policy term, you receive a lump sum maturity amount, and your family is protected with a death benefit throughout the term. It's an ideal solution for those who have a lump sum amount and want to secure it for a future goal.

items: Riders: Accidental Death & Disability Benefit Rider and a New Term Assurance Rider are available.
Tax Benefits: Premium paid can be claimed under Section 80C. Maturity may be tax-free under Section 10(10D) subject to conditions.

content.text: You can surrender the policy after one full year. The value you receive depends on two factors:

items: Guaranteed Surrender Value (GSV): A percentage of the single premium paid (excluding riders/taxes). It's 75% in the first year and 90% thereafter.
Special Surrender Value (SSV): This is a higher value that also depends on the vested bonuses and is determined by LIC based on their performance.

sections.title: Can NRIs Invest in LIC Single Premium Endowment Plan?

content.text: Yes, Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) can absolutely invest in this plan, making it a very popular choice for those looking to invest a lump sum in a secure, India-based instrument. The investment must be made in Indian Rupees (INR) and is subject to FEMA regulations. This is a great way for NRIs to participate in a guaranteed savings plan in India with a single, straightforward payment.
This plan is not for everyone, but it's an excellent fit for specific profiles:

items: Risk-Averse Investors: Individuals who prioritize capital safety over high returns.
Those with Lump Sum Funds: Perfect for retirees with a corpus, people who received a bonus, or NRIs looking to invest a one-time amount in India.
Goal-Based Planners: Parents or grandparents planning for a child's future education or marriage with a fixed, one-time investment.

items.q: What is the difference between LIC Single Premium Endowment Plan 917 and 717?
items.a: There is no major difference. Plan 717 was the offline version, and Plan 917 (and previously 817) are the online versions. The underlying structure and benefits are identical. Our LIC single premium endowment plan calculator online free applies to all these plan numbers.

items.q: What is the return on a â‚¹5 lakh / â‚¹10 lakh single premium policy?
items.a: For a â‚¹5 Lakh policy with a 15-year term, the maturity is around â‚¹8.62 Lakh (IRR ~5.3%). For a â‚¹10 Lakh policy over 20 years, the maturity could be around â‚¹19 Lakh. Use our LIC maturity calculator for precise estimates based on your age and term. You can also compare using our FD vs PPF calculator to see how these returns stack up.

items.q: Is the maturity of LIC single premium plan tax-free under 10(10D)?
items.a: Yes, but with a critical condition for its tax benefit: the maturity is tax-free only if the Sum Assured is at least 10 times the single premium you paid. If the premium is higher relative to the Sum Assured, the proceeds may become taxable.

items.q: What is the IRR of LIC Single Premium Endowment Plan?
items.a: The Internal Rate of Return (IRR) for this plan typically ranges from 5% to 6%, depending on the policyholder's age and the chosen term. This return is often tax-free, making it competitive.

items.q: Can NRIs invest in LIC single premium plan?
items.a: Yes, NRIs can invest in this plan, making it a popular choice for those looking to invest a lump sum in a secure, India-based instrument, subject to FEMA rules.

items.q: LIC single premium vs LIC Jeevan Labh â€” which is better?
items.a: Choose the Single Premium plan if you have a lump sum and want a one-time, hassle-free investment. Choose Jeevan Labh if you prefer to pay premiums over a limited period (like 10-16 years) for a long-term goal. For comprehensive retirement planning, use our retirement corpus calculator and Jeevan Anand calculator to compare all options.

items.q: What is the surrender value calculation method?
items.a: The surrender value is the higher of the Guaranteed Surrender Value (GSV) or Special Surrender Value (SSV). The GSV is a percentage of premiums paid (75% in year 1, 90% thereafter). The SSV is a more favorable value determined by LIC that also includes a portion of vested bonuses.

items.q: Is LIC Single Premium better than FD or PPF?
items.a: It depends on your goal. Use our FD vs PPF calculator to compare returns directly. It's better than an FD for those in higher tax brackets due to its tax-free returns. Compare with our PPF calculator and tax regime calculator to optimize based on your tax situation. It's better than PPF if you have a lump sum to invest instead of making yearly contributions and need life insurance cover included.
